Beta scope: the supported profile and its evidence

What the reference profile supports in the Beta work, adapter by adapter, with the scenario tests behind each claim, the exact refusal text for everything else, and the known limits.

DeveloperOperatorDecision-makerConceptBETA
PrerequisitesA reading of the reference profile page, if you intend to run the supported shape
Reviewed 2026-11-01 · current main branch docs contract

What this page is. It says which parts of CALIBER the Beta work supports, which it does not, and which scenario tests the support claim rests on. It describes main; it does not announce a release, and the Beta release gate (#613) is a separate decision. The alpha scope and alpha install pages stay as the record of the 0.1.0a1 alpha and are not rewritten here. The consolidated Beta scope table (#877) will extend this page; until it does, this page covers the supported profile and the adapter capabilities only.

What "supported" means here#

An adapter is supported only when GET /ajax-api/2.0/mlflow/caliber/capabilities reports it as supported in data.adapters for the deployment you are looking at. That report is derived from the running configuration and from the scenario tests cited below (caliber.features.SUPPORT_EVIDENCE); no setting says "supported", and an adapter with no evidence entry cannot be. The rest of this page is a reading of that report, not a second source for it: a contract test (caliber/tests/test_beta_scope_contract.py) fails when the table, the evidence or the quoted messages below stop matching the code.

Supported does not mean any of these:

  • It is not a release label (nothing here says a Beta is out), a service level or a promise about upgrades, performance or hosting.
  • It does not grant authority. A supported adapter is still behind the authorization, approval and admission checks of its own route and the effect dispatcher.
  • It is not a claim about every integration, connector or MCP backend. Only the two adapters in the matrix below can be supported; every other path is preview, unavailable or refused, and says so.

Every adapter reports exactly one status:

statusmeaning
supportedthe reference profile admits it, the deployment is configured as the cited scenarios were, and the live code still matches what they exercised
previewit can run, but nothing in the supported shape covers it; this is the best an MCP server or an OpenAPI integration can be, and every adapter is here outside the reference profile
unavailableit cannot run in this deployment; the report names the setting that says so, or profile when no setting does

The supported shape#

The supported shape is the reference profile: CALIBER_PROFILE=reference, started from a configuration that passes every rule on that page (PostgreSQL, CSRF on, no development fallbacks, the egress policy on, no MCP allowlist entries, no unlisted plugin, a confined file root, two-person approval and Apply). A process that breaks a rule refuses to start and lists every violation. The default profile, development, is unchanged and supports nothing.

On top of the profile, each adapter needs a little more:

adapteralso needsvariable
document_request_connectorthe background loops on, and the effect reconciler on (both default on)CALIBER_BACKGROUND_TASKS_ENABLED, CALIBER_EFFECT_RECONCILER_ENABLED
release_evaluationthe release area on, its evaluator on, the background loops on, and a real evaluation providerCALIBER_FEATURE_RELEASE_CANDIDATES, CALIBER_WORKSPACE_RELEASE_EVALUATOR_ENABLED, CALIBER_BACKGROUND_TASKS_ENABLED, CALIBER_EVAL_PROVIDER=mlflow

These are the settings the report itself checks. Neither adapter is on after the alpha install: that install runs the development profile, with the release area and the integrations area off, so its report is preview for the connector and unavailable for the rest; with the release area, its evaluator and the integrations area all on it is preview for all four (the matrix below). The workflow queue (CALIBER_WORKFLOW_RUN_QUEUE_ENABLED) is not a condition of either claim.

supported is not a statement that a binding exists. The report does not read the operator's wiring, and the reference profile does not require it. For a protected action to actually reach the document-request connector from a workflow run, the operator also sets:

settingwhat it doesif it is missing
CALIBER_AGENT_STEP_TOOL_BACKENDSmaps a registered tool, by its registry identity, to a backend (document_request) so an agent bound to it runs as a governed stepempty (the default): no agent is governed, and the connector is reached by nothing
CALIBER_EFFECT_CALLBACK_CONNECTORSbinds the connector to the downstream base_url the effect is sent to and the reconciler asks, per projectno binding: connector_unbound, refused before anything is claimed, and nothing is sent

A deployment can therefore report document_request_connector as supported and still send nothing, because no tool is mapped or no connector is bound. Read the worker's trusted inputs before relying on it.

Evidence for each supported adapter#

The report lists these scenario test ids in evidence for a supported adapter, and lists nothing for any other status. Each id is a test function on main; the contract test fails on one that does not exist. Paths are relative to caliber/. All of them are collected by the CI job egi-scenarios-postgres ("EGI scenarios (PostgreSQL)", pytest tests/egi_scenarios, defined in .github/workflows/ci.yml), but they do not all use a database. The last column says which database each one runs on, and the contract test derives it from the test sources: dialect-parameterised is a scenario with a SQLite and a PostgreSQL parameter, and only its PostgreSQL parameter runs on PostgreSQL; no database uses only the HTTP downstream fixture; SQLite from the models builds a SQLite database with Base.metadata.create_all, never PostgreSQL.

adapter idscenariowhat it demonstratesdatabase
document_request_connectortests/egi_scenarios/test_connector_capabilities.py::test_stable_key_mutates_oncethe same idempotency key sent twice commits once at the downstreamno database
document_request_connectortests/egi_scenarios/test_connector_capabilities.py::test_stale_precondition_returns_412_and_no_mutationa write bound to a version that is not current is refused 412 and changes nothingno database
document_request_connectortests/egi_scenarios/test_connector_capabilities.py::test_query_by_key_after_lost_responseafter a response is lost, the request is found by its key at the downstreamno database
document_request_connectortests/egi_scenarios/test_b04_dispatcher.py::test_dispatcher_uses_canonical_approval_and_registered_connectoron a reference-profile app, an approval recorded over the decision route and a real execution-owner lease reach the registered connector once, with an outbox row and a receiptdialect-parameterised
document_request_connectortests/egi_scenarios/test_v07_restart_exactly_once.py::test_kill_after_downstream_commita dispatcher killed after the downstream committed leaves one mutation, found by key and not sent againdialect-parameterised
release_evaluationtests/egi_scenarios/test_v13_release_evaluation.py::test_evaluator_crash_recoversafter an evaluator crash, the provider runs it already observed stay on the evaluation and only the recovered claim settles itSQLite from the models
release_evaluationtests/egi_scenarios/test_v13_release_evaluation.py::test_worker_records_provider_run_before_completion_crasha provider run is recorded before completion, so a crash between the two loses no run identifierSQLite from the models
release_evaluationtests/egi_scenarios/test_v13_release_evaluation.py::test_recovery_before_provider_result_keeps_attempt_historya crash before the provider returns still burns the old claim number and keeps the attempt historySQLite from the models

Two pins keep the claim tied to the code it was shown on: for the connector, the admission record caliber.profile.REFERENCE_CONNECTORS (implementation, capability digest and configuration digest, checked live), and for the evaluator, the implementation WorkspaceReleaseEvaluator and evidence schema version 1. Changing either withdraws the claim (unavailable) until a reviewer confirms the scenarios again.

What the evidence does not cover, stated so the word "supported" is not read wider than it is:

  • The connector scenarios run against a purpose-built downstream fixture (a case record with document requests, started by the tests), not against a customer system. They show the platform's side of the contract: a stable key, a precondition, a read-back by key. A downstream that does not behave like that fixture is outside the claim.
  • The release-evaluation scenarios use a scripted evaluation provider. They prove the claim, recovery and fenced completion of an attempt, not the quality of a real provider's scores. With CALIBER_EVAL_PROVIDER=mlflow the evaluator calls the real provider and reports supported; with fake it reports preview because the scores are simulated.
  • Only two of the five connector scenarios, and none of the release-evaluation scenarios, run on PostgreSQL. test_b04_dispatcher.py (a migrated reference-profile app) and test_v07_restart_exactly_once.py have a PostgreSQL parameter. The three test_connector_capabilities.py scenarios use no database: they show the downstream's stable key, precondition and read-back by key, not the platform's persistence. The release-evaluation scenarios build a SQLite database from the models (no migrations), without a reference-profile app or the capability route, so they show the evaluator's claim, recovery and fencing logic, not PostgreSQL concurrency or lease behaviour, and not the migrated schema.
  • No scenario here proves the whole loop for one workflow end to end under the capability report. The end-to-end governed run (approve, resume, one send, a receipt read back by key) is shown by tests/egi_scenarios/test_b05_governed_worker_wiring.py::test_a_proposal_is_approved_over_http_resumed_and_sent_exactly_once, which is evidence for the controls described below but is not one of the pinned evidence entries. Adding it is a reviewed change to SUPPORT_EVIDENCE, not a documentation edit.

What the worker reaches in the supported shape#

Support of an adapter is not the same as every path to it being open. In the reference profile the workflow-run worker sends a protected action only through a connector whose outcome the platform can read back by key. Today that is:

node or toolwhat the reference profile doesevidence (a control, not a support claim)
a governed agent step bound to a tool the operator mapped to document_request (CALIBER_AGENT_STEP_TOOL_BACKENDS), with the connector bound to a downstream for the project (CALIBER_EFFECT_CALLBACK_CONNECTORS)proposes, parks waiting_approval, and after a different person approves and an operator resumes, sends once and reads the receipt back by keytests/egi_scenarios/test_b05_governed_worker_wiring.py::test_a_proposal_is_approved_over_http_resumed_and_sent_exactly_once
a webhook or API-request node whose exact URL the operator listed in CALIBER_EFFECT_HTTP_VERIFIERSsends to the generic http connector, which is reachable at those URLs only; the http connector is not one of the four adapters and the report claims nothing for ittests/egi_scenarios/test_b05_http_unknown_settlement.py::test_a_listed_webhook_is_sent_once_and_its_2xx_is_confirmed_by_the_lookup
a webhook or API-request node whose URL nobody listedrefused before a proposal is recorded: HTTP effect refused: no_authoritative_verifiertests/egi_scenarios/test_b05_http_unknown_settlement.py::test_a_webhook_whose_url_is_not_listed_is_refused_before_a_proposal_exists
a protected (non-read) registered-tool, OpenAPI or MCP callrefused before a proposal is recorded (a read-class call, such as a GET, HEAD or OPTIONS of a read row or a read-class registered or MCP tool, still runs inline): registered tool effect refused: no_authoritative_verifier, OpenAPI effect refused: no_authoritative_verifier, MCP effect refused: no_authoritative_verifier (these connectors have no lookup by key the platform can call; one shared check produces the sentence, and the tests show it for the HTTP label and the registered_tool verifier)tests/test_governed_worker_wiring.py::test_a_workflow_node_is_refused_before_anything_is_recorded_when_its_backend_has_no_verifier, tests/test_governed_worker_wiring.py::test_the_receipt_verifier_of_a_context_never_allows_an_unverified_connector

Everything the inventory marks as running code, or writing to the host or a database with no dispatcher in front of it, is refused in the reference profile with unsupported_in_reference_profile before anything runs: the python_code, external_app and output_folder nodes, an administrator's registered Python tool, runnable exports, the standalone tool-sandbox service and the host-file built-ins (Refused paths, Executable code). An installed optimizer plugin whose distribution is not in CALIBER_PLUGIN_ALLOWLIST, and CALIBER_WORKFLOW_FILE_ROOT=unconfined, stop the process from starting; a folder_input node, or a file_input node without a managed file, reads only inside the configured file root, and with none configured it is refused (output_folder is refused outright, see above) (Plugins and host paths).

Opt-in, disabled and unavailable: the exact answers#

A feature flag says an area is on, never that it is supported, and turning one on promotes nothing. Each flag is read once at startup, so restart after changing it.

A route of a disabled area answers 404 with reason_code: feature_disabled and the variable to set; the same sentence is the adapter's message in the capability report. Each row below is what the report says, word for word, and the recovery is the variable in disabled_by (profile means no setting changes the answer).

A disabled area (the default install). CALIBER_FEATURE_RELEASE_CANDIDATES unset:

GET /ajax-api/2.0/mlflow/caliber/releases/candidates
404 {"detail": "Release-candidate signoff and workspace releases is disabled in this deployment. Set CALIBER_FEATURE_RELEASE_CANDIDATES=true to enable it.", "status_code": 404, "reason_code": "feature_disabled"}

Release-candidate signoff and workspace releases is disabled in this deployment. Set CALIBER_FEATURE_RELEASE_CANDIDATES=true to enable it.

mcp_servers.message and openapi_integrations.message  (reason_code feature_disabled, disabled_by CALIBER_FEATURE_INTEGRATIONS)
MCP servers and OpenAPI integrations is disabled in this deployment. Set CALIBER_FEATURE_INTEGRATIONS=true to enable it.

Not the reference profile (a development deployment). Recovery: start a process with CALIBER_PROFILE=reference from a configuration that passes it; nothing else promotes the adapter.

document_request_connector.message  (reason_code not_reference_profile, disabled_by CALIBER_PROFILE)
OpenAPI document-request connector is preview in this deployment: it is supported only under CALIBER_PROFILE=reference. Set CALIBER_PROFILE=reference and start from a configuration that passes the profile to use it as a supported path.

Workspace release evaluation is preview in this deployment: it is supported only under CALIBER_PROFILE=reference. Set CALIBER_PROFILE=reference and start from a configuration that passes the profile to use it as a supported path.

release_evaluation.message  (reason_code reference_profile_violations, disabled_by profile)

document_request_connector.message  (reason_code connector_capability_mismatch; connector_not_admitted if the record is gone)

release_evaluation.message  (reason_code evaluator_evidence_mismatch)

The release path, one condition at a time. Recovery is the variable in disabled_by. (CALIBER_EVAL_PROVIDER=auto, the Docker stack's default, is resolved when the settings load: to mlflow when a real language-model provider is configured and to fake otherwise, so the report never sees auto.)

The capability report reads, for a client or the web app, data.adapters.<adapter id> with status, kind, label, reason_code, disabled_by, message and evidence. Read it instead of probing for a 404. data.features is unchanged. The web app's navigation renders these values (#771): a Supported, Preview or Unavailable chip with the message above as its description on MCP Servers, OpenAPI Integrations and Release candidates, and a "Support status" panel that lists all four adapters, including the connector, which has no page. An unavailable adapter that is listed is a disabled item, and anything the server does not report as supported reads as Preview. A visible entry grants no authority; see how the web app renders it.

Known limits#

These are true of main today and are deliberate; each one that has an owner names it.

  • The worker dispatches only two connectors. In the reference profile a production run reaches document_request (through a governed agent step) and http (through a webhook or API-request node at operator-listed URLs). The registered_tool, openapi_http and mcp connectors have no lookup by key the platform can call, so a protected (non-read) call that would use one is refused no_authoritative_verifier before its proposal is recorded; read-class calls still run inline. A protected call the model chooses is proposed (in a governed agent step) or refused (in every other governed loop), never run directly; a plan a caller builds by hand, with no governed context, is not governed (Model-selected tool calls).
  • A permanent unknown has no operator exit yet. A downstream that never shows a request and cannot prove its absence leaves the proposal unknown and its dependents blocked. The attested operator resolution is #1054 and is not delivered; the recovery runbook says what to do and not to do until then.
  • An unknown webhook outcome fails the run. A webhook or API-request node whose effect ends unknown (a timeout after the send, a 5xx, a 2xx the lookup cannot see yet) fails its run; unlike a governed agent step it does not park. The reconciler settles the proposal by the listed lookup without sending again, but settling does not resume the failed run. Read the proposal before running such a workflow again: a new run is a new effect with a new key. Settling the proposal of an ended run, and withdrawing an approved decision that was never consumed, are #1074. A run that is woken after a settlement finds its one effect already committed and fails with HTTP effect was already recorded as committed; not run again, because the response of the original send was never durable.
  • A revoked approver, a lost lease or an unbound connector fails the run with the proposal left proposed (nothing was sent); settling that proposal is #1074.
  • A tool node's own requires_approval gate still asks first, and a governed effect then asks the exact-intent question, so such a node is approved twice.
  • A versioned proposal is sent only through document_request. The platform has no read of its own for another connector's target, so a versioned proposal for any other connector is version_unverifiable.
  • The http read-back is the operator's endpoint. A lookup_url that is not https is refused at startup (http_lookup_cleartext) because the lookup carries no credentials and its answer commits the effect; a 404 from it is never proof that an effect did not happen.
  • Acceptance gates completion for document-request effects only. In the reference profile a run is completed only when every document-request effect it proposed has an accepted decision (#791): the platform reads the downstream's own record of the case when the run finishes, and a run whose effect was committed but whose recorded state is wrong, or could not be read, is failed (acceptance_rejected). An effect of another connector has no criteria set, so a run with only such effects carries no acceptance information, and runs that finished before this are not relabelled. A document request must carry the case version it was proposed against, or its run is rejected.
  • Fifteen protected-effect rows are not routed. The inventory marks them dispatch, but no connector routes them yet, and the matrix records them as unrouted instead of claiming otherwise. They are not refused in the reference profile either, because their reference-profile behaviour has not been decided:
inventory rowswhat they areowner
EP-009, EP-010, EP-013, EP-051, EP-059knowledge-build runs, review-queue enqueue (a platform-database write), output-bucket and object-store writes#1086
EP-070, EP-071, EP-072, EP-075, EP-076, EP-077prompt and release publishing#1087
EP-017, EP-081, EP-090the synchronous run route, Aria's run_workflow tool, and a path with no production caller#1088
EP-034Aria's published-tool call#1063
  • Generated Python can still reach a client. The runnable export routes answer 409 in the reference profile, but the generated text is sealed into the compiled bundle and can leave through compile, get and publish. That is part of #1088; do not read the two 409s as a guarantee that no generated Python reaches a client.
  • Governed effects outside the worker's own graph. Synchronous version runs and the sub-workflows of a worker run have no execution-owner lease and bind no governed context, so the reference profile refuses their protected nodes (and an agent in them that can reach a mapped tool); the development profile runs them on the legacy guarded path. Evaluation, gate and Aria previews are different: they run as previews, with protected tools stubbed, so that refusal does not apply. Refinement and calibration replays are not previews: an agent bound to a mapped tool (or handing off to one) is refused in the replay, so evaluating or calibrating such a workflow scores an error in the reference profile until the replay is given a manifest without that agent.
  • A governed effect inside a fan-out, loop, error boundary, handoff or parallel branch cannot park the run: the run is refused up front (agents) or fails (effects).
  • The capability adapters map is an owner-confirmable decision. Which adapters can be supported, and which scenarios pin them, is caliber.features.ADAPTERS and SUPPORT_EVIDENCE. Adding an adapter, or promoting http or a registered-tool path, is a reviewed change to those tables with its own scenario evidence, and then a change to this page; the owner confirms that decision, and nothing in this page or in a setting makes it.
  • MCP servers stay out of the reference profile. The profile lists no MCP command or host (caliber.profile.REFERENCE_MCP_ALLOWLIST is empty), including the first-party PostgreSQL servers; adding an entry is an ADR 0001 change.
  • Not enforced by the process. The single tenant and region, the object store, at least two projects, origin rules, the database role and cookie flags are stated in ADR 0001 and listed under Not enforced yet; a configuration that passes the profile is the minimum for the supported shape, not the whole of it.
  • Replay observations are a storage/runtime primitive, not the Beta evidence package. B09.3 records immutable, project- and principal-scoped model/read observations with content digests for replay-enabled plans. It does not expose a public replay route or claim that the B14 evidence package exists; see the reference-profile replay notes.

What stays from the alpha#

The alpha pages describe 0.1.0a1 and stay as written, except where a sentence there contradicted main and was corrected. Everything the alpha scope says about the default install still holds: the default profile supports no adapter, the preview areas stay behind their flags (Aria ships on), and enabling a flag accepts that area's preview behaviour and promotes nothing. What the Beta adds is the per-adapter answer above, the reference profile, and the refusal codes, none of which changes a default.
